1_varieties.section_title: Recommended Rice Varieties for Low Country Intermediate Zone

pest_disease_resistance: Moderately resistant to Blast and Brown Plant Hopper
recommended_varieties.special_attributes: High tillering capacity, excellent response to nitrogen fertilization, superior consumer cooking quality.

pest_disease_resistance: Tolerant to iron toxicity and moderate salinity
recommended_varieties.special_attributes: Highly suitable for ill-drained Low Humic Gley soils prone to iron toxicity.
High nutritional and antioxidant value, ideal for traditional red rice markets.

1_varieties.selection_guidance: For well-drained fertile plots, Bg 352 is optimal for maximum yield. For low-lying fields with iron accumulation or poor drainage, select Bg 358 or Bw 367.

first_plowing.timing: 3 to 4 weeks prior to sowing (with initial seasonal rains / canal water issue)
first_plowing.instructions: Invert weeds and crop residues to facilitate anaerobic decomposition. Impound 5-10 cm water for 7-10 days.

second_plowing_and_puddling.instructions: Puddle soil thoroughly using a 2-wheel or 4-wheel tractor with rotovator to break clods and create an impervious hardpan layer that prevents percolation water loss.

bund_maintenance.instructions: Reconstruct and plaster field bunds (Niyara) with fresh puddled mud (height 30cm, width 30cm) to prevent lateral water leakage and seal crab/rat burrows.

leveling.instructions: Final leveling using a wooden leveling board (Poruwa) or laser leveler in shallow standing water (1-2 cm). Uniform leveling is mandatory for effective weed suppression and even seedling emergence.

organic_manure_incorporation.recommendation: Incorporate 4-6 MT/acre of well-decomposed cattle manure, paddy straw, or compost during the first plowing to enhance cation exchange capacity.

3_planting_schedule.establishment_method: Direct Wet Seeding (Row Seeding using 8-row drum seeder or Wet Broadcasting)

seed_treatment_and_sprouting.soaking: Soak certified seeds in clean water for 24 hours.
seed_treatment_and_sprouting.incubation: Drain water and incubate seeds under moist gunny bags in shade for 24 to 36 hours until the white radicle sprout emerges to 1-2 mm length.
seed_treatment_and_sprouting.precaution: Do not allow sprouts to grow longer than 2 mm to avoid mechanical breakage during broadcasting.

3_planting_schedule.spacing: Row spacing of 20 cm x 10-15 cm between hills (for drum seeding or mechanical transplanting).

4_fertilizer_management.organic_integration: Incorporate 1,000 kg/acre well-matured compost or decomposed straw prior to final leveling.

chemical_stages.timing: At final land preparation, immediately before sowing/planting
chemical_stages.application_method: Broadcast evenly and incorporate into the top 5 cm soil layer.
Broadcast onto saturated soil with 1-2 cm shallow water layer.
Drain standing water, broadcast fertilizer, and re-introduce water after 24 hours.

chemical_stages.timing: 50 to 55 Days After Sowing (DAS - for 3.5 month varieties)
chemical_stages.application_method: Apply when 10% of shoots show green ring panicle initiation.

5_water_management.section_title: Water Regime & Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD)
5_water_management.establishment_phase: Days 1-7 DAS: Keep field moist and saturated; avoid standing water to prevent pre-germinated seed rotting.
5_water_management.vegetative_phase: Days 8-45 DAS: Implement AWD. Allow water depth to rise to 3-5 cm, then allow water level to drop naturally until hairline cracks appear on soil before re-flooding.
5_water_management.reproductive_flowering_phase: Days 46-75 DAS: CRITICAL STAGE. Maintain continuous 5 cm standing water from panicle initiation through flowering and milky grain stage. Never allow moisture deficit.
5_water_management.terminal_drainage: Days 76-90 DAS: Completely drain the field 10 to 14 days before harvest to hasten uniform grain ripening and harden the soil for harvesting machinery.

6_weed_control.preventive_cultural: Clean irrigation inlets with mesh screens, maintain 3-5 cm water layer from 8 DAS to inhibit weed seed germination.
6_weed_control.mechanical_weeding: Operate a rotary cono-weeder at 14 DAS and 28 DAS in row-seeded fields to uproot weeds and incorporate weed biomass as green manure.

chemical_herbicide_options.commercial_rate: 60 mL/acre (150 mL/ha) dissolved in 160 L water
chemical_herbicide_options.target_spectrum: Grasses (Echinochloa crus-galli), sedges, and broadleaf weeds.
Broadleaf weeds (Monochoria vaginalis) and sedges (Cyperus iria, Fimbristylis miliacea).

7_harvesting_and_post_harvest.section_title: Harvesting Guidelines, Threshing, and Storage Protocols
7_harvesting_and_post_harvest.maturity_indices: Harvest when 85-90% of panicle grains turn golden straw color and moisture drops to 20-22%. Flag leaves turn pale yellow.
7_harvesting_and_post_harvest.harvesting_procedure: Cut crop 10-15 cm above ground level. Thresh immediately (within 24 hours) using combine harvester or mechanical thresher to avoid fungal moulding.
7_harvesting_and_post_harvest.cleaning_and_drying: Clean winnowed grain to remove chaff and unfilled grains. Sun dry on clean canvas tarpaulins with frequent raking for 2-3 days until moisture drops to 13-14%.
7_harvesting_and_post_harvest.safe_storage: Store in airtight hermetic bags (PICS bags) or clean wooden storage bins in a well-ventilated, pest-proof store elevated on wooden pallets 15 cm above ground.

8_crop_rotation_and_intercropping.section_title: Crop Rotation, Relay Cropping, and Soil Regeneration

recommended_rotations.crop: Mung Bean (Vigna radiata / Green Gram - MI 5, MI 6)
recommended_rotations.cropping_window: Yala Season (Relay sown 7-10 days before Maha paddy harvest or direct sown after harvest)
recommended_rotations.economic_benefit: Generates high supplementary cash income with minimal water requirement.
Drought hardy, excellent high-protein grain and substantial organic green biomass.
Zero-tillage establishment in paddy stubble; high market demand.

8_crop_rotation_and_intercropping.soil_health_benefits: Legume rotation disrupts mono-cropping pest cycles (Brown Plant Hopper, Stem Borer), breaks disease spore perpetuation, improves soil aggregate stability, and saves 20-25 kg Urea/acre in succeeding season.

source: Sri Lanka Department of Agriculture (DOA) - Paddy Crop Management Compendium (Circular RRDI-2023-01)
